welcome.title: Welcome to Handy Tool
welcome.body: Speak, and your words are typed wherever your cursor is. Your speech is turned into text on this PC.
welcome.steps: This short setup asks which languages you speak, suggests a speech model for them, and shows your shortcuts and microphone. Every step can be skipped, and everything can be changed later in the settings.

languages.title: Which languages will you speak?
languages.body: Pick every language you use. The suggested speech models then understand all of them.

model.body: Three good fits for {{languages}}: the most accurate, a balance of both, and the fastest. Pick one and it downloads while you finish the setup; you can switch later on the Models page.
model.bodyAny: Three good fits: the most accurate, a balance of both, and the fastest. Pick one and it downloads while you finish the setup; you can switch later on the Models page.

shortcuts.title: Your shortcuts
shortcuts.body: These work right away. Keep them, or click one and press the keys you want instead. Each shows its default, so you can always go back to it.
shortcuts.transcribe: Press once to start, again to stop.
shortcuts.cancel: Stops a recording without typing anything.
shortcuts.more: More shortcuts (Transcribe & Submit, pause, undo last word, …) are on the Shortcuts page.
shortcuts.remote: Working in Remote Desktop? The Remote Desktop setup on the Setups page keeps the shortcuts you choose on this PC (Windows).

microphone.title: Which microphone?
microphone.body: Default follows your system's default microphone. Pick another one if you speak into a headset or a USB microphone.

try.title: Try it
try.body: Press {{keys}}, say a sentence, then press it again. Your words appear below.
try.listening: Listening… press {{keys}} again when you're done.
try.downloading: {{model}} is still downloading ({{percent}}%). Try it once it's ready — or go on with Next.
try.noModel: No speech model chosen yet, so there's nothing to try. Go on with Next and pick one on the Models page.

done.title: You're ready
done.howTo: Press {{keys}}, speak, and press it again: the text is typed where your cursor is.
done.downloading: {{model}} is downloading ({{percent}}%) — it is used as soon as it's ready.
done.noModel: No speech model chosen yet: pick one on the Models page.

suggested.title: Want to fine-tune more?
suggested.body: Everything already works with good defaults, so you don't need these now. If you like, one of these setups walks you through more.

catalog.description: Guided setups ask a few questions and set things up for you. Every step can be skipped.

basic.title: Basic setup
basic.description: Your languages, a speech model suggested for them, the basic shortcuts, your microphone, and a quick try — the same guide as on the first start.

jumper.title: Jumper
jumper.description: Let Handy Tool paste your dictation into the right field for you: it remembers the places you type in (a chat box, a document, a field in a remote session), puts the text there automatically wherever you are, and jumps back to them with a key.

remote.title: Remote Desktop shortcuts
remote.description: Keep Handy Tool's shortcuts working while a Remote Desktop session has the keyboard: switch on Shortcut Keeper and choose which shortcuts stay on this PC; every other key still goes to the remote.

postProcessing.title: Post-processing
postProcessing.description: Let an AI model clean up or reshape what you dictate (punctuation, filler words, a structure, a translation), with its own shortcut.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: How the recording pill and the live text box look: the pill's place and size, its sound bars, how it shows progress, and the live text box, with every choice shown moving before you pick it.

goal.title: What is the Jumper for?
goal.body: In many apps (a chat, an email, a document, a remote desktop) Handy Tool can put your dictation straight into the right text field for you. The Jumper remembers those fields, so the text lands there automatically, even when you are in another window, and a key takes you back to them. Pick what you want from it; you can change it later on the Jumper page.

jump.title: Jump back with a key
jump.detail: Press a shortcut and the remembered field is in front of you again, ready to type.

land.title: Have my dictation land there
land.detail: Wherever you are when a take ends, the text goes into the remembered field, so you can read something else while you dictate.

both.title: Both
both.detail: Jump there with a key, and dictation lands there too.

mouse.title: Remember the mouse position too?
mouse.body: In browsers and apps like Discord or Teams, Windows sees only the whole window, not the text box inside it. With the mouse position remembered, Handy clicks back into the exact box.

no.title: No, just the field
no.detail: Enough for most desktop apps (Word, Notepad, email).

yes.title: Yes, the mouse position too
yes.detail: For web pages and chat apps. Handy clicks where the mouse was when you showed the place.

places.title: Show me the place
places.body: Press the button, then click into the text field you want within {{seconds}} seconds. Handy remembers the field that has the focus when the time is up. You can add more places.

shortcuts.title: Your shortcuts
shortcuts.body: Set remembers the field you are in right now; Jump takes you back to it. Keep the defaults, or click one and press the keys you want.

test.title: Try it
test.bodyJump: Click Jump there: the remembered field should come to the front, ready to type.
test.bodyLand: Click Jump there to check each place. Then dictate anywhere: when the take ends, the text lands in Place 1.
test.none: No place was remembered. You can add places on the Jumper page with their Set shortcuts.

done.title: The Jumper is ready
done.body: Your places are kept after a restart. Everything else (more slots, remote sessions, tracking where text last landed) is on the Jumper page.

prompt.title: What should the AI do with your words?
prompt.body: After a take, an AI model rewrites the text the way you ask. Pick what it is told; you can edit it later under {{postProcessingPage}}.
prompt.ownDetail: Your own instructions, for example "Translate to English" or "Write it as a bullet list".
prompt.ownPlaceholder: Tell the AI what to do with the text, e.g. Fix the punctuation and remove filler words. Keep my wording.

provider.title: Which AI should do it?
provider.body: An online one needs a key from its website; one running on this PC (LM Studio, FLM) needs only its model. The same list is under {{providersPage}}.

shortcut.title: Your post-processing shortcut
shortcut.body: Dictate with this shortcut when you want the AI to rework the text; your other shortcuts stay plain.

try.title: Try it
try.body: Edit the sample if you like and run it through the AI with your prompt.
try.sample: so um I think we should uh meet on tuesday no wait wednesday at like three and bring the the report

done.title: Post-processing is ready
done.body: Dictate with the post-processing shortcut and the AI's version is pasted. The prompt, the AI and more options are under {{postProcessingPage}}.

appearance.name: Appearance setup
appearance.sample: Hi Anna, I will send the draft numbers on Friday so everyone can comment before the review next week.

intro.title: Your recording pill
intro.body: While you dictate, this pill shows what Handy Tool is doing. Here is what its parts are for. The next steps show every choice moving side by side, so you can compare them before you pick.
intro.t: T: the live text box, which shows your words while you speak. Click the T to switch the box on or off at any time; it glows while the box is on.
intro.bars: Sound bars: your voice. They move while the microphone hears you.
intro.pause: Pause: stops listening for a moment; press it again to go on. Shown when the Pause button is switched on.
intro.cancel: ×: cancels the take. Nothing is transcribed or pasted.

theme.title: Light or dark?
theme.body: The colours of every Handy Tool window. The recording pill stays dark in all of them.
theme.system: Follows Windows, and changes when Windows does.

position.title: Where should the pill appear?
position.body: While you dictate, at the bottom or the top of the screen, or not at all.
position.bottom: In the middle, just above the taskbar.
position.top: In the middle, at the top of the screen.
position.none: No pill. The tray icon still shows that it is recording.

size.title: How big should the pill be?
size.body: Bigger is easier to see on a large or high-resolution screen.

bars.title: How wide should the sound bars be?
bars.body: The bars in the middle of the pill show your voice.

narrow.title: Narrow
narrow.detail: 62 px, with more room around them.

progress.title: How should it show the progress?
progress.body: After you stop, the pill shows how far the transcription is.
progress.line: A thin line fills along the bottom.
progress.ring: A glowing light runs round the edge and stays lit up to the figure.
progress.lap: A thin light keeps circling the edge; the figure is in the text.

glow.title: How strongly should it glow?
glow.body: The glow around the progress light. You can fine-tune it later with Glow Strength.

liveText.title: Show your words while you speak?
liveText.body: The live text box sits next to the pill and shows what you say as you talk; the T on the pill switches it on and off at any time. With a Parakeet model the words in the box become your text: the take is not transcribed again as a whole at the end, only its last part is caught up, so the text is ready sooner but can be a little less accurate. With other models the box is only a preview: the whole take is transcribed again when you stop.

last_words.title: Last words
last_words.detail: One line with your newest words.

full_text.title: Whole text
full_text.detail: Everything so far; the box grows as you talk.

liveText.remote: {{model}} runs online and gets the audio only after you stop, so the live text box can't work with it. Pick a model that runs on this PC on the Models page first.

width.title: How wide should the box be?
width.body: A wider box needs fewer lines for the same text.

textSize.title: How big should the text be?
textSize.body: The size of the words in the live text box.

quiet.title: When you speak too quietly
quiet.body: If your voice is too quiet for the model to hear well, the pill can tell you.

box.title: In a box under the pill
box.detail: The pill keeps its sound bars.

pill.title: In the pill
pill.detail: In place of the sound bars, for a moment.

done.title: Your look is set
done.body: Your pill and live text box are set. More is in the settings: General › App for the pill (size, sound bars, progress, glow and colour, with a moving preview), and General › Transcription for the live text box (width, text size, lines, fade). You can also run this setup again from Setups.

color.title: Which colour should it glow in?
color.body: The colour of the progress light and its glow, the glowing T and the sound bars. For any other colour, use Progress Colour in General › App.

appearance.title: Appearance setup
appearance.text: See every look moving before you pick it: the pill, its progress and the live text box.

jumper.title: Jumper setup
jumper.text: Have your dictation pasted into the right field automatically: set up your places and their shortcuts step by step, with a test at the end.

postProcessing.title: Post-processing setup
postProcessing.text: Let an AI clean up or reshape what you dictate: pick what it should do and which AI, step by step, with a try at the end.

intro.title: Your shortcuts in Remote Desktop
intro.body: Remote Desktop Connection and the Windows App take every key while their session has the keyboard, so Handy Tool's shortcuts stop working there. Shortcut Keeper keeps the shortcuts you choose on this PC: they run Handy Tool here, and every other key, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and Alt+Tab included, still goes to the remote. Windows only; not Citrix.

switch.title: Switch on Shortcut Keeper
switch.body: It watches the keyboard only while a Remote Desktop session is in front, and never stores or sends what you type. Type Chinese, Japanese or Korean? Say so here too.

shortcuts.title: Choose what stays on this PC
shortcuts.body: Tick Keep on this PC next to the shortcuts you use while working in a session. Paste last transcription pastes into the session once you let go of its keys.
shortcuts.more: Every other shortcut has the same box on the Shortcuts page.

try.title: Try it
try.body: Click into your Remote Desktop session, full screen if you like, and press a ticked shortcut: it runs Handy Tool here. The line below says Active while the session has the keyboard. If a shortcut still goes to the remote, click outside the session and back in.

done.title: Your shortcuts are kept
done.body: Change which shortcuts stay on this PC any time on the Shortcuts page, under Shortcut Keeper.

shortcut.title: Handy Tool Shortcuts
shortcut.description: Configure keyboard shortcuts to trigger speech-to-text recording
shortcut.altGrConflict: Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so this shortcut may fire when you type AltGr characters such as ą or ó. A chord without Ctrl+Alt avoids that.
shortcut.conflict: Also set for: {{names}}. Only one of them works at a time; give one of them other keys.
shortcut.singleKey: This key alone fires the shortcut in every app, so typing it there may not work. Adding Ctrl or Alt avoids that.

transcribe.name: Record/Transcribe Shortcut
transcribe.description: Press once to start recording and again to finish; the transcription is delivered into the window that had focus. Default: Ctrl+Space. It follows Transcription Mode and the Paste Method on Transcription — for hold-to-record instead, use Push-to-Talk Shortcut.

cancel.name: Cancel Shortcut
cancel.description:
**Cancels the take that is in progress.**

**Default:** escape.

What cancelling actually does is decided by Cancel behavior on the General page, and the tray Cancel item follows the same setting:

- Finish, save to history only: still transcribes and stores the text, but delivers nothing to your window.
- Discard recording: throws the audio away.

pause.name: Pause / Resume
pause.description: Pauses the recording in progress, or resumes it. Active only during a take while the pause button is on. Default: None.

undo_word.name: Undo Last Word
undo_word.description: Removes the last word of a live take; hold to keep removing words. Active only during a live take while Undo last word is on. Default: Ctrl+Backspace.

toggle_live_text_box.name: Live Text Box On/Off
toggle_live_text_box.description: Switches the live text box on or off, like the T button on the recording overlay. Default: None.

cycle_capture_source.name: Cycle Sound Source
cycle_capture_source.description: Switches what recordings capture, in turn: Microphone, System audio, Microphone + system audio. The recording overlay shows the new source for a moment. During a recording it switches that recording from that moment on, unless the recording started with System audio alone; then the new source applies to the next one. Windows only. Default: None.

transcribe_ptt.name: Push-to-Talk Shortcut
transcribe_ptt.description:
**Hold this shortcut to record, release it to stop.** The microphone goes cold on release, so anything you say afterwards cannot leak into the text.

**Default:** Ctrl+Shift+Space.

It has its own Transcription Mode (PTT) and its own Paste Method (PTT), so push-to-talk can behave differently from Record/Transcribe Shortcut.

transcribe_with_post_process.name: Post-Processing Hotkey
transcribe_with_post_process.description: Optional: A dedicated hotkey that always applies AI post-processing to your transcription.

type_text.name: Type Text Shortcut
type_text.description:
**Types whatever is in the Keyboard Typer box into the window that currently has focus.** Press it again, or Escape, to cancel.

**Default:** ctrl+shift+F11.

It starts after about a second rather than waiting out Start delay, because pressing a shortcut means you are already in the target window — the Go button is the one that uses the full countdown.

transcribe_and_submit.name: Transcribe & Submit Shortcut
transcribe_and_submit.description: Finish recording, paste the transcription, then press the submit key. Works even if recording was started with another shortcut.

anchor_set.name: Set Anchor
anchor_set.description:
**Captures the text field you currently have focused as the Hot 1 destination.**

**Default:** ctrl+shift+F1.

On its own it delivers nothing: set 'Jump slot action on finish' to 'Jump / deliver to slot' with the slot set to Hot 1 (Transcription) to make your next transcription land there. Password boxes and Handy's own windows are refused.

anchor_jump.name: Jump to Anchor
anchor_jump.description: Brings the Hot 1 window and field back into focus and pastes nothing — a 'back to my draft' key. Default: ctrl+shift+F2. If 'Save mouse position' is on for this slot the pointer moves back too; nothing happens if the slot is empty or its window has closed.

jump_set_slot_1.name: Set Jump Slot 1
jump_set_slot_1.description:
**Memorizes the field you currently have focused as static slot 1**, replacing whatever it held.

**Default:** ctrl+alt+shift+1.

The slot is only a bookmark until something uses it: jump to it with 'Jump to Slot 1', or point a flow's 'Jump slot action on finish' (Transcription) at Slot 1 to have transcriptions delivered there.

jump_set_slot_2.name: Set Jump Slot 2
jump_set_slot_2.description: Memorizes the field you currently have focused as static slot 2, replacing whatever it held. Default: ctrl+alt+shift+2. Jump back with 'Jump to Slot 2', or point a flow's 'Jump slot action on finish' (Transcription) at Slot 2 to have transcriptions delivered there.

jump_set_slot_3.name: Set Jump Slot 3
jump_set_slot_3.description: Memorizes the field you currently have focused as static slot 3, replacing whatever it held. Default: ctrl+alt+shift+3. Jump back with 'Jump to Slot 3', or point a flow's 'Jump slot action on finish' (Transcription) at Slot 3 to have transcriptions delivered there.

jump_set_slot_4.name: Set Jump Slot 4
jump_set_slot_4.description: Memorizes the field you currently have focused as static slot 4, replacing whatever it held. Default: ctrl+alt+shift+4. Jump back with 'Jump to Slot 4', or point a flow's 'Jump slot action on finish' (Transcription) at Slot 4 to have transcriptions delivered there.

jump_slot_1.name: Jump to Slot 1
jump_slot_1.description: Brings static slot 1's window and field into focus and delivers nothing — pure navigation. Default: ctrl+alt+1. If 'Save mouse position' is on for this slot the pointer is restored too; nothing happens if the slot is empty or its window has closed.

jump_slot_2.name: Jump to Slot 2
jump_slot_2.description: Brings static slot 2's window and field into focus and delivers nothing — pure navigation. Default: ctrl+alt+2. If 'Save mouse position' is on for this slot the pointer is restored too; nothing happens if the slot is empty or its window has closed.

jump_slot_3.name: Jump to Slot 3
jump_slot_3.description: Brings static slot 3's window and field into focus and delivers nothing — pure navigation. Default: ctrl+alt+3. If 'Save mouse position' is on for this slot the pointer is restored too; nothing happens if the slot is empty or its window has closed.

jump_slot_4.name: Jump to Slot 4
jump_slot_4.description: Brings static slot 4's window and field into focus and delivers nothing — pure navigation. Default: ctrl+alt+4. If 'Save mouse position' is on for this slot the pointer is restored too; nothing happens if the slot is empty or its window has closed.

failurePanel.title: Shortcuts not registered
failurePanel.description: These shortcuts are inactive. Change a chord or retry after resolving the conflict.

errors.reset: Failed to reset shortcut to original value
errors.registrationFailed: Some shortcuts could not be registered and are inactive: {{bindings}}. Another app may already be using them — pick a different combination in Settings.

shortcut.altGrConflictLayout: A keyboard you use for {{layouts}} types a character with AltGr+{{key}}. Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so typing that character may fire this shortcut instead. A chord without Ctrl+Alt avoids that.
shortcut.altGrConflictSpace: A keyboard you use for {{layouts}} types characters with AltGr, and AltGr is often still held for the space after one. Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so that space may fire this shortcut instead. A chord without Ctrl+Alt avoids that.

pauseButton.label: Pause button
pauseButton.description:
**Adds a pause button to the recording overlay**, so one take can span a break: while paused nothing is recorded, and resuming continues the same take.

**Default:** Off.

Once it is on, a Pause shortcut can be set below. After 10 minutes paused the microphone is released (its indicator goes out) until you resume.

undoWord.label: Undo last word
undoWord.description:
**Removes the last word of a live take** each time you press its shortcut; hold it to keep removing words. You see each word disappear from the live text box.

**Default:** Off; the shortcut is Ctrl+Backspace, active only during a live take.

It cuts the recording back to where that word started, so the word stays out of the final text too. Needs a live take (Live mode or the live text box) and a Parakeet model — other engines give no word positions.

liveTextBox.label: Live text box
liveTextBox.description:
**Shows what you are saying in a small box next to the recording overlay**, updated about every 1.5 seconds.

**Default:** Off. The T button on the overlay switches it too.

While it is on, every take runs in Live mode. Text before a pause is fixed and only the last few seconds are re-read, so it stays quick on a busy PC. With a Parakeet model the text in the box is your transcript: when you stop, only what you said after the last fixed words is transcribed and added — the take is not transcribed a second time. With other models the box is only a preview and the whole take is transcribed again when you stop. Needs a model that runs on this PC.

remoteModel.title: The live text box doesn't work with {{model}}
remoteModel.worksWith: It needs a model that runs on this PC, because remote engines only get the audio after you stop. It works with: {{models}}.
remoteModel.noLocal: It needs a model that runs on this PC, because remote engines only get the audio after you stop. Download one on the Models page.

liveTextAfterStop.label: Show the text as it's transcribed
liveTextAfterStop.description:
**When a take without the live text box stops, the box appears and the transcript is typed into it as it comes in** — the parts already transcribed at once, the rest as soon as it is ready. Just to watch: the text is delivered as usual.

**Default:** Off.

It uses the live text box's style and width. With the live text box on, every take is live and shows its text anyway.

liveTradeoffs.title: Live transcription: good to know
liveTradeoffs.accuracy: With a Parakeet model the text you see is the text you get, so it is a little less accurate than Post-Recording, most of all on long stretches without pauses; Post-Recording gives the most accurate text. Other models transcribe the whole take again when you stop, so the box is only a preview and a long take takes longer to finish.
liveTradeoffs.cpu: It uses more CPU and battery while you talk.
liveTradeoffs.undo: Undo last word works only with Parakeet models.

liveTextMode.title: Live text shows
liveTextMode.description:
**One line with the newest words, or the whole take so far** in a box that starts at one line and grows as you talk, up to 40% of the screen height; after that the oldest lines slide away.

**Default:** Last words.

liveTextFade.label: Fade when you stop talking
liveTextFade.description:
**The live text fades away a few seconds after you stop talking**, so words you are done with don't stay on screen. Your next words bring it back.

**Default:** Off.

liveTextWidth.title: Box width
liveTextWidth.description: How wide the live text box is. A wider box needs fewer lines for the same text. **Default:** Medium.

liveTextHeight.title: Box height
liveTextHeight.description: How many lines the live text box shows in Whole text mode before the oldest lines slide out. **Default:** Medium (6 lines).

liveTextSize.title: Text size
liveTextSize.description: How big the text in the live text box is. **Default:** Normal.

anchor.title: Anchor & Deliver
anchor.deliveryFailed: Anchored delivery failed: {{reason}}. Your text is on the clipboard and the anchor was kept.

status.title: Current anchor
status.description:
**Shows what this hot slot currently points at**, with Test (jump there without delivering anything) and Clear. A 'Remote ✓' badge means the target matched your Remote match strings.

**Default:** No anchor set — click into a text field and press this slot's Set Anchor shortcut to arm it.

An anchor is never used up by a delivery: it stays until you clear it or its window closes.

keep.label: Keep anchor after delivery
keep.description: Leave the anchor armed after a successful delivery instead of clearing it, for repeated dictation into the same field.

returnFocus.label: Return focus after delivery
returnFocus.description: Switch back to the window you were using once the text has been delivered.

idle.title: Jump slot action on start
idle.description:
**What this shortcut also does with the slot chosen on the left at the moment you press it to start a take.**

**Default:** Do nothing — which is why the slot picker starts greyed out.

- Jump / deliver to slot: moves you into that remembered field before you speak.
- Set slot to current focus: records where you are right now.
- Clear slot: forgets it.

Windows only.

stop.title: Jump slot action on finish
stop.description:
**What this shortcut does with the slot chosen on the left when the take finishes.**

**Default:** Do nothing.

- Jump / deliver to slot: sends the transcription into that remembered field instead of wherever you have drifted to, so you can read something else while dictating.
- Set slot to current focus, Clear slot: run only after the text has been delivered.

Only jump on finish if started the same way, on the Jumper page, can narrow when a jump is allowed. Windows only.

anchor.deliveryFailedHistoryOnly: Anchored delivery failed: {{reason}}. Your clipboard was left untouched and the anchor was kept — the text is in History. {{recovery}}

pasteMethod.title: Paste method
pasteMethod.description: The paste keystroke used by the Transcribe & Submit Shortcut only, so the one app you dictate-and-send into can behave differently from everything else. Default: Clipboard (Ctrl+V). It overrides Paste Method for this flow — set it to Clipboard (Shift+Insert) if that app's message box ignores Ctrl+V.

submitKey.title: Submit key
submitKey.description: The key pressed immediately after this flow pastes, to actually send the message or run the command. Default: Enter. This flow always submits — Auto Submit does not apply to it — so choose Ctrl+Enter or Super+Enter for apps where plain Enter only inserts a new line.

idleBehavior.title: When no recording is active
idleBehavior.description:
**What happens when you press the Transcribe & Submit Shortcut while nothing is being recorded.**

**Default:** Start a recording — one press starts, the next pastes and submits.

Choose Do nothing to make this key a pure finisher: you start takes with the Record/Transcribe Shortcut and press this one only when you want that result pasted and sent.

clipboard.title: Clipboard
clipboard.description:
**This flow's own clipboard policy, independent of Clipboard Handling:** restore your existing clipboard after pasting, or deliberately leave the sent transcription on it.

**Default:** Don't Modify Clipboard.

Useful when normal dictation should leave your clipboard alone but you want a copy of everything you sent — or the other way round.

jumperPasteDelay.title: Paste delay after jump (Windows)
jumperPasteDelay.description:
**Extra wait between a jump bringing the target window to the front and the paste keystroke** — a window activated a heartbeat ago still swallows keystrokes.

**Defaults:** Local apps 300 ms, Remote desktop 600 ms. Remote match strings on the Jumper page decides which applies.

It only ever runs on a real jump: when you are already in the target, pasting stays instant. Both dropdowns are shared by Transcribe and Transcribe & Submit.

jumperSubmitDelay.title: Submit delay before Enter (Windows)
jumperSubmitDelay.description:
**Extra wait between delivering the text and pressing the submit key** — a target that is still committing the text loses the Enter.

**Defaults:** Local apps 300 ms, Remote desktop 600 ms. Remote match strings on the Jumper page decides which applies.

- Runs after a real jump.
- Always runs for a remote desktop target, even when you were already in it: a remote session needs a round trip to commit the text whether or not Handy activated the window.
- Only an already-focused local target submits instantly.

Changed in 1.3.0: before that, an already-focused remote target did not wait at all, so the Enter could submit a partial dictation.

language.title: Language
language.description:
**Tells the engine which language you are speaking.** Naming it is usually more accurate than Auto and stops short takes being detected as the wrong language.

**Default:** Auto.

It applies to the model named in this card's heading. With Translate to English on, it means the language you speak, not the language you get back.
language.descriptionUnsupported: Parakeet model automatically detects the language. No manual selection is needed.

pushToTalk.label: Push To Talk
pushToTalk.description: Hold to record, release to stop

pasteMethod.title: Paste method
pasteMethod.description:
**How the Paste Last Transcription shortcut puts the text into the focused window** — separate from the Paste Method on Transcription, so you can tune it for the one stubborn target.

**Default:** Clipboard (Ctrl+V).

- Clipboard (Shift+Insert): try it in a terminal.
- Direct: types the characters instead of pasting.
- None: only places the text on the clipboard so you can paste it by hand.

clipboard.title: Clipboard
clipboard.description:
**Whether re-pasting puts your previous clipboard back afterwards, or deliberately leaves the transcription on it.**

**Default:** Don't Modify Clipboard — copies the text, pastes it, then restores what you had.

Pick Copy to Clipboard to keep the words available after the re-paste. Either way only clipboard text is saved and restored, so an image or copied file is lost.

cancelBehavior.title: Cancel behavior
cancelBehavior.description:
**What cancelling does to the recording in progress** — covers the Cancel Shortcut, the tray "Cancel" item and 'handy --cancel'.

**Default:** "Finish, save to history only": stops and transcribes the take, keeps it in History with its audio, and delivers nothing at all — no paste, no clipboard change, no submit key, no jump.

Choose "Discard recording" if you would rather a cancelled take were thrown away without being transcribed or stored.

updates.title: Updates

checks.label: Check for updates automatically
checks.description: Check public GitHub releases once a day.
checks.privacy: Checking for updates sends nothing about you—there is no telemetry, analytics, or account—and only reads one public file from the project's GitHub releases.

silent.label: Install updates silently
silent.description: Close, update, and reopen during the allowed window. Off by default.
silent.portableDescription: Unavailable in portable mode. Replace the portable folder to update it; Handy Tool will never run the NSIS installer here.

time.label: Silent update time
time.description: Center of the allowed local-time window.

jitter.label: Daily randomization
jitter.description: Choose a different time within this many minutes each day.

updates.upToDate: Handy Tool is up to date.
updates.portableUnsupported: Portable copies cannot update in place. Download the latest portable release.

conflicts.title: Some shortcuts share the same keys
conflicts.description: Only one action can work on a key combination, so only one of each pair does. Give one of the shortcuts marked Conflict other keys, or clear it.

altGrWarning.label: Show hints for AltGr shortcuts
altGrWarning.description:
**Shows a hint next to shortcuts that AltGr may also type with.** Windows reports AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so a shortcut like Ctrl+Alt+O may fire when you type ó with AltGr, and the character may not arrive. On Windows the hint appears only when one of your keyboards types something with AltGr on that key (or AltGr+Shift, for a chord with Shift), and names the language the keyboard belongs to.

**Default:** On. Switch it off if you never type characters with AltGr.

keeper.title: Shortcut Keeper
keeper.summary: Keeps the shortcuts you tick on this PC while a Remote Desktop session has the keyboard, so they run Handy Tool here instead of reaching the remote. All other keys go to the remote as before.
keeper.label: Keep chosen shortcuts on this PC in Remote Desktop (Windows)
keeper.description:
**Remote Desktop takes every key while its session has the keyboard** (in full screen, or when Windows key combinations go to the remote computer), so Handy Tool's shortcuts stop working there. With this on, the shortcuts you tick with Keep on this PC run Handy Tool here. Every other key, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and Alt+Tab included, still goes to the remote.

**Works with:** Remote Desktop Connection (mstsc) and the Windows App, on Windows. Not with Citrix: use Citrix Workspace's own setting for Windows key combinations instead.

**Not yet:** push-to-talk and Undo last word, which act while the key is held. Paste last transcription can be kept: it pastes into the session when you let go of the keys.

**Best effort:** if a kept shortcut stops working, click outside the session and back in.

**Privacy:** Handy Tool watches the keyboard only while a Remote Desktop session is in front, reacts only to the shortcuts you ticked, and never stores, logs or sends what you type.

**Default:** Off.

cjk.label: I type Chinese, Japanese or Korean
cjk.description:
**Only then do you need the Ctrl+Space note.** On Chinese, Japanese and Korean setups Ctrl+Space switches the input method; a kept Ctrl+Space no longer reaches the remote for that. Switch this on and a kept Ctrl+Space shows that note.

**Default:** Off.

status.waiting: On. Waiting for a Remote Desktop session to have the keyboard.
status.active: Active: a Remote Desktop session has the keyboard, and the ticked shortcuts stay on this PC.
status.higher_integrity: This Remote Desktop session runs as administrator, so Windows keeps Handy Tool out of it. Start the Remote Desktop client without administrator rights to use Shortcut Keeper.
status.needs_restart: Restart Handy Tool to use Shortcut Keeper: the other keyboard implementation ran in this session.
status.unavailable: Works only with the default keyboard implementation (Tauri), set in the debug settings (Ctrl+Shift+D).

keeper.checkboxHint: Ticked: this shortcut runs Handy Tool on this PC while a Remote Desktop session has the keyboard.
keeper.turnOnFirst: Switch on Shortcut Keeper at the top of this page first.

reasons.needs_hold: Acts while the key is held, which Shortcut Keeper cannot handle yet.
reasons.unbound: No keys are set for this shortcut.
reasons.win_key: Shortcuts with the Windows key cannot be kept: the remote would still see the Windows key and open its Start menu.
reasons.alt_only: Alt shortcuts without Ctrl cannot be kept: the remote would still see Alt and open its menu bar. Add Ctrl to the shortcut.
reasons.modifier_only: Needs a main key besides the modifier keys.
reasons.unknown_key: This key cannot be kept. Use a letter, digit, F-key, Space, Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, Insert, Delete, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down or an arrow key.
reasons.rdp_combo: Remote Desktop itself uses Ctrl+Alt+Home (connection bar) and Ctrl+Alt+End (Ctrl+Alt+Delete inside the session). Kept on this PC, the remote no longer gets it.
reasons.layout_switch: The remote still sees Ctrl and Shift without a key, which switches its keyboard layout if Ctrl+Shift is set for that there.
reasons.ctrl_space: Ctrl+Space switches the input method on Chinese, Japanese and Korean setups. Kept on this PC, the remote no longer gets it.

models.description:
**Choose which speech model transcribes your dictation** — models differ in accuracy, speed and how much memory they hold while loaded.

**Default:** nothing selected on a fresh install; onboarding downloads and selects your first model.

Your choice also decides whether Language and Translate to English are offered on the General page, and the Translator uses this same model whenever its Batch model is left on "Same as dictation (default)".
models.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete {{modelName}}? You will need to download it again to use it.
models.deleteActiveConfirm: {{modelName}} is your active model. Deleting it will stop transcriptions until you select a new model. Are you sure?

jumper.windowsOnly: The Jumper is available on Windows only.

remoteMatch.title: Remote match strings
remoteMatch.description:
**Marks remote desktop windows by name.** A delivery target whose app, window class or control class contains one of these fragments (case-insensitive) is treated as a remote desktop.

Remote targets use the Remote value of 'Paste delay after jump (Windows)' and 'Submit delay before Enter (Windows)' on Transcription instead of the Local one. Since 1.3.0 an already-focused remote window is classified too, not only a jump target — which is what makes the submit delay apply there.

**Default:** msrdc, mstsc, Citrix.

Add the process name your RDP or Citrix client uses if deliveries into it keep getting swallowed. An empty list treats every target as local.
remoteMatch.badgeTooltip: This target matches a remote match string, so it uses the Remote timing values.

optionsMoved.title: Delivery options
optionsMoved.description:
**Not a setting — a signpost.** What a jump actually does with a slot is configured per flow on Transcription:

- 'Jump slot action on start'
- 'Jump slot action on finish'
- 'Track last output location'
- 'Return focus after delivery'

Each exists once for Transcribe and once for Transcribe & Submit.
optionsMoved.hint: Configured in the Transcribe and Transcribe & Submit groups on Transcription.

slot.title: Static slot {{index}}
slot.description:
**Shows what this numbered slot points at**, with Test (jump there without delivering anything) and Clear.

**Default:** no target. Focus a field you keep coming back to, press this slot's Set shortcut (ctrl+alt+shift+1 … 9), and jump back any time with ctrl+alt+1 … 9.

A slot remembers a window and a field — not a browser tab or a text cursor position — and it survives deliveries.

persist.label: Remember slots across restarts
persist.description:
**Remembers every slot's target across app restarts.**

**Default:** Off.

Windows cannot keep a window handle across a restart, so Handy saves each slot's identity (application plus window and field type) and re-finds the matching window at startup and again the moment you use the slot. A saved slot whose app is not running shows red until it reappears.

track.label: Track last output location
track.description:
**Makes a slot follow you.** After this flow pastes a transcription, the slot chosen in 'Save location into' is overwritten with the field the text actually landed in, so your next jump to that slot returns to the last place you dictated.

**Default:** Off.

Transcribe and Transcribe & Submit track independently, and the capture happens before any 'Return focus after delivery'. Windows only.

slot.title: Save location into
slot.description: Which jump slot 'Track last output location' overwrites after every delivery by this flow. Default: Hot 1. Point it at a static slot (Slot 1 to Slot 9) if you do not want automatic tracking to keep overwriting the hot anchor you set by hand with Set Anchor.

saveCursor.label: Restore mouse cursor position
saveCursor.description: After this flow delivers a transcription, remember the mouse cursor position and move the pointer back there when you jump. Independent of the other flow's switch; the position mode below is shared between both flows.
saveCursor.perSlotDescription: Also records the mouse pointer position when this slot is set or tracked, and moves the pointer back there when you jump to this slot — after the paste, so it cannot disturb delivery. Default: Off. Turn it on for a slot on another monitor so keyboard and mouse arrive together; it enables this slot's own 'Cursor position mode' below, and every slot has its own pair of switches.

mode.title: Cursor position mode
mode.description:
**How this slot's saved pointer position is measured.**

**Default:** App-relative (follows the window) — restores the same spot inside the target window even after it has been moved, resized, or dragged to a monitor with a different DPI.

Pick Screen-absolute (exact coordinates) for something that never moves, such as a fixed dashboard. The dropdown is greyed out until 'Save mouse position' is on for this slot.

returnFocus.label: Return focus after delivery
returnFocus.description:
**After a delivery that had to jump, focus goes back to the window you were in when the delivery started** — captured automatically, with no slot to set up.

**Default:** On.

It is conditional: if you switched windows yourself while Handy Tool was working, it leaves you where you chose to be. Each flow decides this separately. Windows only.

requireSameFlow.label: Only jump on finish if started the same way
requireSameFlow.description:
**When on, a flow's 'Jump slot action on finish' fires only if the take was started and finished with the same shortcut.**

**Default:** Off.

Example: start with Transcribe and finish with Transcribe & Submit and you get no jump — the paste and the submit still happen, only the jump is gated. Turn it on if mixing the two shortcuts keeps teleporting you somewhere unexpected.

enabled.label: Watch folders
enabled.description:
**Transcribes every new .wav, .mp3, .m4a, .mp4 (its audio track), .aac, .flac, .ogg (Opus) or .opus file that lands in a watched folder** into a .txt file next to it, using your current model, Language and Translate to English settings.

**Default:** off.

Files already sitting in a folder when watching starts are deliberately left alone. The folders themselves are chosen under Add a folder.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description:
**Who gets the speech engine when a folder file and your own dictation want it at the same moment.**

**Default:** Live dictation first — the batch pauses at the next segment boundary the instant you press record and resumes afterwards, so no batch progress is lost.

- Folder batch first: the batch keeps running and your live text arrives a little later.
- First come, first served: the file in progress finishes, then your take runs before the next file starts.

model.title: Batch model
model.description:
**Which speech model transcribes the files in your watched folders.** Models marked with a globe can also translate to English, which needs Translate to English switched on.

**Default:** Same as dictation (default) — reuses whatever is selected on the Models page.

Pick a different local model and it loads into a slot of its own next to the dictation model: batch work on one engine, dictation still instant on the other. The cost is extra memory, which Unload batch model after can hand back.

unload.title: Unload batch model after
unload.description:
**How long the Translator's own copy of the batch model stays in memory after the queue goes quiet.** Unloading returns the RAM or VRAM; keeping it loaded avoids a reload when the next file arrives.

**Default:** Never (keep loaded — fastest start).

It only has an effect when Batch model names a local model different from your dictation model — otherwise the main Unload Model setting governs.

status.title: Status
status.description: What the Translator is doing right now. Finished transcripts are written next to the audio file with the same name and a .txt extension.

paused.processing: paused while a recording is finishing

folders.title: Folders
folders.emptyDescription: Add a folder to start watching it for new recordings.
folders.addDescription: Opens a folder picker; from then on any new audio file that appears in that folder is queued and its transcript is written beside it as a .txt. Default: your Handy recordings folder is added for you the first time the Translator starts. Adding a folder does nothing until Watch folders is on, and whatever is already in the folder is ignored — only files that arrive afterwards are transcribed.

model.title: Model
model.description:
**Which speech model transcribes the file.** Models that aren't downloaded yet are listed too; pick one and download it first.

**Default:** your dictation model, and the one you pick is remembered. Another model loads beside your dictation model, so dictation stays ready, and unloads again when the file is done.

transcribe.title: Transcribe a file

choose.title: Choose an audio file
choose.description:
**Transcribes an audio file you pick**: WAV, MP3, M4A, MP4 (the audio track of a video), AAC, FLAC or Ogg Opus (.ogg, .opus), such as a phone recording, with the model chosen above and your language settings.

The file is cut at its pauses into pieces of up to about 40 seconds, and each piece is transcribed once: no live text, no second pass. The original file is only read, never changed.

transcribe.empty: No speech was found in this file.

saveText.title: Save the text
saveText.description:
**Where the transcript is saved as a .txt**, named after the audio file. If the name is taken, a number is added; nothing is overwritten.

**Default:** Ask every time: a pop-up asks when you pick a file, and can remember your choice. The text is shown to copy either way.

keepAudio.title: Keep a copy of the audio
keepAudio.description:
**Copies the audio file into the folder below**, next to its text, so you still have it if the original is moved or deleted.

**Default:** off. The original is never moved or changed.

folder.title: Folder
folder.description:
**Where the text goes when it is saved in Handy's folder, and where audio copies go.**

**Default:** a "files" folder inside Handy's own data folder.

ask.title: Where should the text be saved?
ask.dontSaveHint: The text is still shown to copy and kept in the list.
ask.rememberHint: You can change it later under Save the text.

log.title: Transcribed files
log.empty: Nothing transcribed yet. Every file you transcribe here is listed with its text.

microphone.title: Microphone
microphone.description: The input device Handy records from. It takes effect on your next take, with no restart. Default: the system default device — set it explicitly when you switch between a headset and the built-in array, and use the reset button to go back to the system choice.

micKeepWarm.title: Keep microphone ready
micKeepWarm.description:
**Keeps the microphone open for a few minutes after each take**, so the next one starts at once instead of waiting for an idle microphone to wake up (up to about a second).

**Default:** Off — the microphone closes as soon as a take ends.

While it stays open, your system microphone indicator stays lit. Hidden when Always-On Microphone is on.

micWarmup.title: Wait for the microphone to warm up
micWarmup.description:
**After an idle microphone starts, the recording overlay keeps showing "Starting mic..." until it has really warmed up.** Some microphones start much quieter and fade in over a second or so; words spoken into that were dropped as noise. The wait is the average of this microphone's last few cold starts, measured by the app itself.

**Default:** On.

Only a cold start waits — a microphone kept ready starts at once. Hidden when Always-On Microphone is on.
micWarmup.notMeasured: Not measured yet — it measures itself on the next cold start.

tooQuiet.title: Warn when you speak too quietly
tooQuiet.description:
**When you speak too quietly for your words to be kept, the recording overlay says "Too quiet — speak up" for a moment**. It reacts to sound that is almost speech and clearly above the room's noise for about 0.7 s; silence, music and typing don't set it off. It can't tell when words were heard wrong — the live text box shows that.

**Default:** On.

box.title: Show it in its own box
box.description:
**"Too quiet — speak up" appears in a small box just under the recording overlay, and the overlay keeps its sound bars.** With the overlay at the bottom of the screen, the box sits in the gap above the taskbar, so it never covers the live text box. Off: the overlay shows it in place of its sound bars (with the pause button on, longer translations get cut off there).

**Default:** On.

audioFeedback.label: Audio Feedback
audioFeedback.description: Plays a short cue when recording starts and a different one when it stops, so you know the microphone is hot without looking at the screen. Default: Off. Turning it on enables Output Device and Volume below; the two cue sounds can be swapped for your own files via Sound Theme on the Debug page.

outputDevice.title: Output Device
outputDevice.description: Where the start and stop cues play — it does not affect which microphone records or where other apps send their audio. Default: the system default device. Point it at your headset so the cues do not come out of the speakers; the control stays greyed out until Audio Feedback is on.

volume.title: Volume
volume.description: How loud the start and stop cues are, from 0 to 100 percent. Default: 100%. Turn it down if the cues are startling in a headset; it changes only Handy's own cue sounds, and stays greyed out until Audio Feedback is on.

tokenCountProviders.hint: Providers for the Token Count page. Tip: the model only selects the tokenizer — pick the smallest model of the family you care about (e.g. qwen3:0.6b counts the same as qwen3:8b but loads in a fraction of the time). Anthropic and Gemini counting endpoints are free; local servers are queried with a 1-token probe.
tokenCountProviders.refreshModels: Load model list from the endpoint

crashResilientRecording.label: Crash-Safe Recording
crashResilientRecording.description:
**Encodes your speech to compact Opus files on disk while you talk**, instead of holding it all in memory — a crash, a forced update or a flat battery still leaves a recording, which is repaired and added to History on the next launch.

**Default:** On.

Switching it off records uncompressed audio, which Full data (with compressed audio) backups deliberately leave out.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Sets the colour theme for every Handy Tool window, including the recording overlay and the floating transcription window. Default: System, which follows your Windows light/dark setting and keeps tracking it; Light and Dark pin one palette and ignore later OS changes.

startHidden.label: Start Hidden
startHidden.description:
**Starts Handy Tool with no window on screen** — it goes straight to the system tray and dictation works immediately.

**Default:** Off.

Pair it with Launch on Startup so the app is ready at sign-in without a window appearing. Leave Show Tray Icon on: the tray is then your only way to open the window.

autostart.label: Launch on Startup
autostart.description: Registers Handy Tool to launch automatically when you sign in to Windows. Default: Off. Combine it with Start Hidden so it comes up quietly in the tray instead of opening its window.
autostart.portableDescription: This portable copy can create a Windows startup entry outside its folder. Default: Off.
autostart.portableConsentMessage:
Portable autostart writes a machine-wide Windows startup entry. It is not part of the portable folder and points to this folder. If you move, rename, or unplug it, Windows will try to start an application that is not there. If Handy Tool is also installed normally on this PC, this replaces that copy's startup entry. This is the one thing a portable copy leaves behind; turning autostart off removes it again.

Enable autostart?

showTrayIcon.label: Show Tray Icon
showTrayIcon.description:
**Shows the Handy Tool icon in the system tray**, where it signals idle, recording and transcribing. On Windows a click opens the window; its menu (right-click) has settings, the last transcript and Quit.

**Default:** On.

Careful: with it off, closing the main window quits the app instead of hiding it — and if Start Hidden is also on, there is nothing on screen to click.

overlay.title: Overlay Position
overlay.description: Shows a small overlay while you dictate so you can see that Handy Tool is listening and then transcribing, placed at the bottom or the top of the screen. Default: Bottom. Choose None to turn it off when it covers something you need or gets in the way of a full-screen app.

reopenLastPage.title: Reopen Last Page
reopenLastPage.description:
**Opens Handy Tool on the page you had open when you closed it** (for example History) instead of General.

**Default:** On.

overlaySize.title: Overlay Size
overlaySize.description:
**How big the recording overlay is**, and the "Too quiet" box under it. Larger is easier to see on a big or high-resolution screen.

**Default:** Normal.

soundBarsWide.title: Wide Sound Bars
soundBarsWide.description:
**Wider sound bars on the recording overlay:** 2.5 px bars and gaps (77.5 px) instead of 2 px (62 px).

**Default:** Off.

progressStyle.title: Progress Style
progressStyle.description:
**How the recording overlay shows how far a transcription is:** a thin line filling along its bottom; a glowing light running round its edge from the bottom centre, lit behind it up to the figure; or a thin light circling the edge, one lap every 1.6 seconds (the figure is in the text). With reduced motion the circling light becomes the line.

**Default:** Line.

progressLineGlow.title: Glowing Line
progressLineGlow.description:
**The progress line glows like the light around the edge**, its aura reaching past the overlay's edge.

**Default:** Off. Only with Progress Style: Line along the bottom.

progressGlow.title: Glow Strength
progressGlow.description:
**How strongly the progress light glows**: "Light around the edge", and the line while "Glowing Line" is on. 0% turns the glow off, 200% doubles it.

**Default:** 100%.

pasteMethodPtt.title: Paste Method (PTT)
pasteMethodPtt.description: The same choice as Paste Method, but used only by the Push-to-Talk Shortcut, so hold-to-talk can deliver differently from your normal dictation key. Default: Clipboard (Ctrl+V). Change it when the app you push-to-talk into needs a different paste keystroke from the app you dictate into all day.

pasteMethod.title: Paste Method
pasteMethod.description:
**The keystroke ordinary dictation uses to deliver the text into the focused window.**

**Default:** Clipboard (Ctrl+V).

- Clipboard (Shift+Insert): for a terminal or remote viewer that ignores Ctrl+V.
- Direct: types the characters instead of pasting.
- None: sends nothing — combined with Clipboard Handling set to Copy to Clipboard, the text is left ready for you to paste by hand.

Push-to-talk ignores this setting and uses Paste Method (PTT).

typingTool.title: Typing Tool
typingTool.description: Chooses which Linux input-injection utility backs the Direct paste method. Default: Auto (Recommended), which probes for the best tool installed. It appears only in the planned Linux build and is never shown on Windows.

clipboardRestoreDelay.title: Clipboard restore delay
clipboardRestoreDelay.description:
**Extra wait before your previous clipboard text is restored after a paste**, on top of the built-in 50 ms.

**Default:** Off (instant).

It does nothing unless this group's clipboard setting (Clipboard Handling here, or Clipboard under Transcribe & Submit) is Don't Modify Clipboard.

Raise it to about 1 s if a Citrix or RDP session pastes your old clipboard instead of what you just said — remote sessions only fetch the clipboard after the paste keystroke has arrived.

clipboardHandling.title: Clipboard Handling
clipboardHandling.description:
**What is on your clipboard after ordinary dictation pastes.**

**Default:** Don't Modify Clipboard.

- Don't Modify Clipboard: the transcript is there only long enough to paste, then your previous clipboard text is restored.
- Copy to Clipboard: deliberately leaves the transcript there.

Honest limit: only text is restored, so a copied image or file is lost — and Clipboard restore delay has no effect unless this is set to Don't Modify Clipboard.

autoSubmit.title: Auto Submit
autoSubmit.description:
**Sends a submit key about 50 ms after every ordinary paste**, so a dictated chat message sends itself.

**Default:** Off.

- Apps disagree about which key sends: try Ctrl+Enter if plain Enter only adds a new line.
- Ignored when Paste Method is None.
- Does not govern the Transcribe & Submit Shortcut, which always sends its own Submit key.

translateToEnglish.label: Translate to English
translateToEnglish.description: Asks the model for English output instead of transcribing what you said in its own language. Default: Off. Leave Language set to the language you actually speak — this toggle only appears for models that support translation.
translateToEnglish.descriptionUnsupported: Translation is not supported by the {{model}} model.
translateToEnglish.unsupported: Not available for the selected transcription model.

modelUnload.title: Unload Model
modelUnload.description:
**Frees the RAM or VRAM the transcription model holds once it has sat unused this long.** The next take then pays a few seconds to reload it.

**Default:** Never (keep loaded — fastest start), the right choice if you dictate throughout the day. Pick a timeout if you dictate in bursts and want the memory back in between.

The Translator's separate batch engine is not covered here; it is released by Unload batch model after.

transcriptionMode.title: Transcription Mode
transcriptionMode.description:
**Live shows the text building up while you speak; Post-Recording records quietly and transcribes in the background.**

**Default:** Post-Recording.

With Crash-Safe Recording on (the default), Post-Recording transcribes the take piece by piece while you talk, so the text is ready moments after you stop; with it off, the whole take is transcribed when you stop. In Live mode with a Parakeet model the text you saw is the text you get, and only the end of the take is caught up at stop; with other models Live mode transcribes the whole take again when you stop. This governs Record/Transcribe Shortcut only, and API transcription models always behave as Post-Recording.

transcriptionModePtt.title: Transcription Mode (PTT)
transcriptionModePtt.description: The same Live-or-Post-Recording choice, applied only to Push-to-Talk Shortcut. Default: Live — deliberately the opposite of Transcription Mode, because held takes are short and the preview shows up almost at once. With a Parakeet model the delivered text is the live text, with the end of the take caught up at stop; with other models it comes from a final pass over the whole recording.

gpuDevice.title: GPU Device
gpuDevice.description:
**Which graphics adapter local Whisper transcribes on, or CPU-only processing.**

**Default:** Auto (Default). An adapter that fails to start falls back to Auto rather than breaking transcription.

Change it to keep a busy discrete card free or to work around a bad driver. It takes effect the next time the model loads, and it only appears on Windows while a Whisper model is selected.

url.title: API URL
url.description:
**Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible speech server, including the version prefix.** Handy appends /audio/transcriptions to it, so http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 becomes http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions.

**Default:** empty — fill it in before choosing API Transcription (OpenAI-compatible) on the Models page, or the take fails.

This engine always uploads the whole recording as one WAV file when you stop, so Transcription Mode has no effect on it.

apiKey.title: API Key
apiKey.description: Bearer key sent with every upload; leave it empty for a local server that does not check one. Default: empty. It is stored unencrypted in your settings file and is included in backups.

model.title: Model
model.description:
**The model id your endpoint expects, sent verbatim with the upload** — whisper-1 for OpenAI, or whatever name your own server gives its model.

**Default:** empty, which sends an empty model field; set it if your endpoint requires one.

When Language is Auto this engine sends English, so pin Language if you dictate in another language.

customWords.title: Custom Words
customWords.description:
**Names, products and jargon the engine keeps getting wrong.** After each transcription Handy finds similar-sounding words and substitutes your spelling instead.

**Default:** empty.

Add whole words as you hit them. If it starts correcting things you did not mean, lower Word Correction Threshold on the Debug page.
customWords.placeholder: Add a word, then press Enter

mcp.description:
**Runs a small local server so Claude (app and Code) and the handy command can use Handy's own tools:** count tokens, type text into the focused window, read History, run model tests and edit providers.

**Default:** Off. Switching it on starts the server straight away on 127.0.0.1 with the Port and Token below — never on a network interface.

Honest caveat: the token is stored in plain text in your settings file, so any program running as you can read it and drive the app.
mcp.claudeApp: Claude app (HTTP) — add a custom MCP server with this URL:
mcp.cliHint: Copies Handy's own executable onto your PATH as handy, so you can run handy model-test, handy token-count or handy mcp --stdio from any terminal against the running app. Default: not installed. The command talks to the app over the same local server, so it only works while Enable MCP & CLI server is on; it is unavailable in portable mode.

costReport.title: Transcription cost report
costReport.description: Per-recording cost (real USD from OpenRouter) and length, summarized by week, month, and year. Download the full report — every recording plus the summaries — as a CSV.

llmProviders.hint: One registry of providers — name, endpoint, key, model and cost per million tokens — shared by Token Count, Model Testing and Post-processing. Each slot keeps a stable id (#1, #2, …) that those screens reference, so a change here applies everywhere; unticking Enable this provider removes the slot from all three. Default: the three local slots are on and every cloud slot is off until you paste a key.
llmProviders.persistPriceHint: Keep this price even when the model changes (don't auto-fill from OpenRouter)

url.title: API URL
url.description: OpenRouter API root that speech requests go to, including /api/v1. Default: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 — leave it as is unless you go through a proxy. Handy sends nothing at all while this or API Key is empty.

apiKey.title: API Key
apiKey.description:
**Your OpenRouter key (openrouter.ai/keys), used only by this speech engine** — separate from any OpenRouter entry under Registered LLM Providers.

**Default:** empty — without it the take fails rather than sending an unauthenticated request.

Dictating with this engine uploads your audio to OpenRouter and costs money per recording; the real amount is recorded in History and in Transcription cost report.

model.title: Transcription model
model.description:
**The OpenRouter model id, typed by hand.**

- Transcription route: openai/whisper-large-v3 style ids.
- Chat route: an audio-capable chat model such as google/gemini-2.5-flash.

**Default:** blank, which falls back to openai/whisper-large-v3.

It has to match Endpoint — a mismatch usually comes back as an empty transcription rather than an error.

route.title: Endpoint
route.description:
**Which OpenRouter endpoint the audio goes to.**

**Default:** Transcription (Whisper-style).

- Transcription (Whisper-style): posts to the dedicated speech endpoint.
- Chat model (Gemini / GPT-4o-audio): puts the audio inside a chat message — the only way models that are not speech models will accept it.

It must agree with Transcription model. Translate to English is honoured on the Chat route only.

format.title: Audio format
format.description:
**How the audio is encoded before upload.** Opus is roughly ten times smaller than WAV, which matters on a tether or a hotel connection.

**Default:** Opus — smaller (recommended).

This only applies when Endpoint is Chat model (Gemini / GPT-4o-audio). The Transcription (Whisper-style) route always sends WAV, because Whisper-style models reject Opus.

clipboardRestoreDelayRemote.title: Clipboard restore delay for remote desktops
clipboardRestoreDelayRemote.description:
**Overrides the clipboard restore delay when you dictate into a remote desktop session.**

**Default:** not set — inherits the normal delay above. 1 s is a sensible starting point.

- Why it exists: RDP and Citrix fetch clipboard data on demand AFTER the paste keystroke arrives, over a slower channel than a local app, so restoring too early hands the remote app whatever you had copied before.
- Honest cost: a longer restore leaves the transcript on your clipboard longer, widening the window in which clipboard history and clipboard managers can capture it.

Which windows count as remote comes from the match list on the Jumper page. Windows only.

preserveTranscriptions.label: Keep transcriptions when recordings are removed
preserveTranscriptions.description: Retention deletes only the audio file and keeps the transcription text forever. On by default. With this on, the history limit caps how many recordings keep their audio, not how many transcriptions you keep.

enable.title: Add text before
enable.description: Insert your own text at the start of every delivered transcription. The history entry keeps the plain transcript.

newline.title: New line after it
newline.description: Put the transcription on its own line below your text. On by default.

enable.title: Add text after
enable.description: Append your own text at the end of every delivered transcription. The history entry keeps the plain transcript.

newline.title: New line before it
newline.description: Put your text on its own line below the transcription. On by default.

captureSource.title: Sound source
captureSource.description: What a recording captures: your microphone, the sound your computer is playing, or both mixed together. Recording system audio lets Handy transcribe the other people on a call. Windows only.

systemAudioDevice.title: Playback device to capture
systemAudioDevice.description: Which speakers or headphones to record from. Following the system default is usually right, and it keeps working when Windows switches devices for a call.

systemAudioDelay.title: System audio delay
systemAudioDelay.description: How far the system audio lags your microphone. The right value depends on your hardware — a USB headset, a Bluetooth link and an HDMI monitor each buffer differently. If the other person's words land late relative to yours, raise this.

systemAudioGain.title: System audio level
systemAudioGain.description: How loud the system audio is relative to your voice. Raise it if the other person comes out too quiet to transcribe; lower it if they drown you out. Only the system audio is scaled — your microphone is never touched.

progressColor.title: Progress Colour
progressColor.description:
**The colour of the pill's glowing parts:** the progress light and its glow (the line, the light around the edge and the circling light), the glowing T and the sound bars. Chosen with three sliders: Hue (which colour), Saturation (how vivid) and Lightness. The swatch shows the result; the reset button brings back the default.

**Default:** cyan.

pillPreview.title: Preview
pillPreview.description: **The recording pill as the settings around it make it, moving:** recording on the left (the T lit while the live text box is on, the sound bars) and transcribing on the right, its progress running from 0 to 100% over and over with your progress style, glow and colour, at your Overlay Size.

appleIntelligence.description: Runs fully on-device. No API key or network access is required.
appleIntelligence.requirements: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS Tahoe (26.0) or later. Apple Intelligence must be enabled in System Settings.
appleIntelligence.unavailable: Apple Intelligence is not available on this device. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS Tahoe (26.0) or later with Apple Intelligence enabled in System Settings.

model.descriptionCustom: Provide the model identifier expected by your custom endpoint.
model.descriptionDefault: Choose a model exposed by the selected provider.

temperature.title: Temperature
temperature.description: Lower is more deterministic and firm (0 = most literal); higher is more creative.

api.registryNote: The provider's API key, model, and base URL are configured in Advanced settings › LLM providers › Registered LLM Providers.

disableThinking.description: Send think: false to the model. Speeds up responses but may reduce instruction-following for thinking models (e.g. Qwen3).

prompts.createFirst: Click 'Create New Prompt' above to create your first post-processing prompt.

currentAudio.idle: Start recording to see live transcription
currentAudio.streamingHint: Text appears progressively as you speak only when the shortcut you pressed—Transcribe or Push-to-Talk—is set to Live and you’re using a local model.

history.title: History

stats.title: Recording statistics
stats.description: How many recordings you made and how long they were, by day, week, month and year. The all-time line also counts the recordings History has since cleaned up. Download the full list as a CSV.

search.regexActive: Query is being treated as a regular expression

history.deleteError: Failed to delete entry. Please try again.

logDirectory.title: Log Directory
logDirectory.description:
**Opens the folder holding the file logs** — the first place to look when something failed without saying why.

Logs rotate at 10 MB and older files are kept rather than overwritten, so the evidence survives the restart that usually follows a problem.

How much detail lands here is set by Log Level on the Debug page, which defaults to Debug and can include transcript fragments.

logLevel.title: Log Level
logLevel.description: Sets how much detail is written to the log files; the console output is not affected. Default: Debug. Lower it to Info if you do not want dictation content on disk — at Debug and Trace, transcript fragments and prompt previews can appear in the files you open from Log Directory on the About page.

soundTheme.label: Sound Theme
soundTheme.description: Chooses which pair of cue sounds plays when a recording starts and stops. Default: Marimba. You will only hear anything while Audio Feedback is on (General page), and Custom appears in this list only once both custom start and stop WAV files exist in the app-data resources folder.

wordCorrectionThreshold.title: Word Correction Threshold
wordCorrectionThreshold.description: How eagerly a transcription is rewritten to match the entries in Custom Words on the General page. Default: 0.18. Raise it if names and jargon still come back mangled; lower it if Handy Tool starts replacing words you actually said — with Custom Words empty, this slider does nothing at all.

historyLimit.title: History Limit
historyLimit.description:
**How many transcriptions History keeps before the oldest ones are removed along with their audio.**

**Default:** 5 entries — deliberately low, so raise it if you expect to look things up days later.

It only has an effect while Auto-Delete Recordings is set to Keep latest, and entries you mark with Save transcription are kept regardless and never counted against it.

recordingRetention.title: Auto-Delete Recordings
recordingRetention.description:
**Automatic cleanup of History:** when an entry ages out, both its row and its audio file are deleted.

**Default:** Keep latest — keeps only the newest entries allowed by History Limit (5 by default).

- 3 days, 2 weeks, 3 months: keep everything from that period instead.
- Never: delete nothing at all.

Cleanup runs after each new transcription is saved and again when you change either setting. It always spares entries marked with Save transcription, and only ever removes audio files Handy Tool created itself.

alwaysOnMicrophone.label: Always-On Microphone
alwaysOnMicrophone.description:
**Keeps the microphone stream open between takes** instead of opening it each time you press a recording shortcut.

**Default:** Off.

Turn it on if the start of a take is clipped: a microphone that has been idle can take most of a second to wake, and the overlay shows Starting mic... until it does. The price: your system microphone indicator stays lit the whole time Handy Tool is running, not just while you dictate.

clamshellMicrophone.title: Clamshell Microphone
clamshellMicrophone.description:
**A different input device for when a laptop lid is closed**, for docked machines whose built-in microphone is unusable that way.

**Default:** none — Microphone on the General page is always used.

Closed-lid detection is macOS-only and macOS builds are still planned, so this has no effect on the Windows build.

postProcessingToggle.label: Post Processing
postProcessingToggle.description:
**Turns on the optional AI clean-up pass**; its hotkey, provider and prompt appear right below this switch.

**Default:** Off.

Your normal Record/Transcribe Shortcut is unaffected: clean-up runs only on the separate Post-Processing Hotkey, and History keeps the raw transcription next to the processed one.

muteWhileRecording.label: Mute While Recording
muteWhileRecording.description: Mutes your system audio for the length of each recording, so music or a video on your speakers cannot bleed into the microphone. Default: Off. Turn it on if you dictate over speakers rather than a headset; the sound comes back on its own when the recording stops.

appendTrailingSpace.label: Append Trailing Space
appendTrailingSpace.description: Adds one space to the end of every delivered transcription, so two dictations in a row do not come out as "...one.Two". Default: Off. Turn it on if you dictate in short bursts into the same field; leave it off where a stray space matters, such as a search box or a terminal command.

keyboardImplementation.title: Keyboard Implementation
keyboardImplementation.description:
**Which backend registers Handy Tool's global shortcuts with the operating system.**

**Default:** Tauri Global Shortcut.

Switch to Handy Keys when a shortcut you set never fires because another program already owns the combination or Windows refuses the registration. All shortcuts are re-registered when you switch, and the change rolls back if that fails.
keyboardImplementation.bindingsReset: Keyboard shortcuts were incompatible and reset to defaults

pasteDelay.title: Paste Delay
pasteDelay.description:
**How long Handy Tool waits after putting the transcription on the clipboard before it sends the paste keystroke.**

**Default:** 60 ms. Raise it if a slow app pastes your previous clipboard contents instead of the new text.

This is a different wait from Paste delay after jump (Windows), which only applies when a Jumper slot has just activated another window.

backup.description: Export your Handy Tool data as a compressed archive. Downloaded models and large uncompressed audio (WAV/FLAC) are always excluded.
backup.configHint: Exports your settings plus the transcription history database (timestamps, text, cost, duration) and no audio, so the file stays small. Use it before a big configuration change, or to carry your shortcuts, providers and prompts to another machine. The archive is not encrypted and it contains your provider API keys and MCP server token in plain text — treat the file as a secret.
backup.fullHint: Everything in the configuration export plus your compressed recordings (.opus/.ogg) — a much larger file, and it still contains your API keys in plain text. Downloaded models, uncompressed WAV/FLAC audio and in-progress chunk files are always excluded, so takes recorded with Crash-Safe Recording switched off appear as history rows with no audio in the archive.
backup.restoreHint: Pick a Handy Tool backup archive (.tar.gz) and tick what to bring back — Configuration & history (settings, history DB) and Recordings (audio files) are independent, so you can take one without the other, and both start ticked. Only entries Handy Tool recognises are extracted, and what is restored replaces what you have now. Restoring settings or history needs a restart: use the Restart Handy Tool now button that appears, or the running app will overwrite them on its next save.
backup.restartHint: Restart Handy Tool to load the restored settings/history (until then the running app may overwrite them).

version.title: Version
version.description: The build of Handy Tool you are running; quote it whenever you report a problem. Windows x64 is the only build released — macOS and Linux are planned, and the Jumper features are Windows-only even after that. Nothing here checks for a newer version by itself; use Updates when you want to look.

appDataDirectory.title: App Data Directory
appDataDirectory.description:
**Opens the single folder holding everything Handy Tool keeps:**

- settings (including your provider API keys and prompts) in a JSON file
- transcripts in a SQLite database
- recordings, downloaded models and rotated logs

**Default:** %APPDATA%\pr.handy on a normal Windows installation.

Nothing in it is encrypted by Handy Tool — file-system permissions are the only protection — so this is also the folder to copy, or clear, when you hand the machine on.

handy.title: Handy
handy.description: The original open-source speech-to-text app this project is built on
handy.details: Handy Tool is a fork of Handy, created by CJ Pais (github.com/cjpais/Handy, handy.computer). It was taken over at upstream v0.8.1 (March 2026) and has been further developed independently by Patrick R. Huge thanks to CJ and the Handy contributors for the foundation this project stands on.

whisper.title: Whisper.cpp
whisper.description: High-performance inference of OpenAI's Whisper automatic speech recognition model
whisper.details: Handy Tool uses Whisper.cpp for fast, local speech-to-text processing. Thanks to the amazing work by Georgi Gerganov and contributors.
