appLanguage.description:
**Switches the whole interface, including the tray menu, to one of the 17 shipped languages.**

**Default:** your Windows display language, falling back to English when that language is not shipped.

This is the interface language only — the language you speak is set by Language on the General page.

flm.windowsApplicationControlBlocked: Windows Application Control blocked flm.exe because it is not signed. The NPU engine is unavailable. Choose a different transcription model.
flm.notInstalled: FLM is not installed. Install FastFlowLM to use NPU-accelerated models.

tokenCount.title: Token Count
tokenCount.placeholder: Paste text here to count tokens...
tokenCount.countAllTitle: Count with every enabled provider one at a time — right when slots share one local service that must load/unload each model
tokenCount.countAllParallelTitle: Query every enabled provider at the same time — fastest when services are independent
tokenCount.chipDisabled: Not configured — switch it on with Enable this provider under Advanced settings › LLM providers › Registered LLM Providers.

options.cl100k_base: Counts the text in the box with the exact GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 tokenizer (cl100k_base), entirely on this machine — nothing is uploaded and it works offline. Use it for OpenAI models up to GPT-4; for newer ones use o200k (GPT-4o).
options.o200k_base: Counts the text in the box with the exact GPT-4o and o1 tokenizer (o200k_base), entirely on this machine — nothing is uploaded and it works offline. Use it for current OpenAI models; older GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 models tokenize with cl100k (GPT-4).
options.estimate: A rough local guess of about 1.3 tokens per word, with no tokenizer and no network call. Use it when the model you care about has no exact counter here, and treat it as a ballpark only — it is deliberately left out of the "Δ vs smallest" column so a rough number cannot skew the comparison between the exact counters.

keyboardTyper.description:
**Sends this text to the focused window as individual simulated keystrokes**, so it works where pasting is blocked — remote consoles, VM viewers, password prompts.

- Go: starts the Start delay countdown (default 10 s) so you can click into the target window first.
- Type Text Shortcut: when you are already in the target, typing begins after about a second.

The text lives in memory only — it is never written to your settings, to History, or to the logs.

shortcut.hint: (change it on the Shortcuts page; press it again to cancel)

modelTesting.description:
**Sends one prompt to every model you tick under Run and lays the answers out side by side** with token counts, cost and round-trip time. Models ticked under Judge then score all of those answers using your judge prompt.

**Default:** nothing selected and both prompts empty.

The list comes from Advanced settings › LLM providers › Registered LLM Providers, so a run uses your own API keys — your prompt leaves this machine and, for paid providers, costs real money.
modelTesting.noProviders: No chat-capable providers configured. Add one in Advanced settings › LLM providers › Registered LLM Providers.

whatsNew.intro: The new and changed things of the last updates. Show me opens the setting.

updateIcon.title: The update icon shows where you stand
updateIcon.description: The icon next to the version at the bottom left is always there now. A green check means the last check found nothing newer, a cyan arrow means an update is available, and a grey arrow means there is no recent result (not checked yet, or the check failed): click it to check. Clicking the version opens the details.

keeperPasteLast.title: Paste last transcription works in Remote Desktop
keeperPasteLast.description: Shortcut Keeper can now keep Paste last transcription on this PC: inside a Remote Desktop session it pastes your last transcription into the session when you let go of its keys. A new Remote Desktop setup on the Setups page walks you through choosing the shortcuts to keep. Windows only.

calmerHints.title: Calmer hints next to shortcuts
calmerHints.description: Shortcuts that may not work everywhere now show a question mark, and ones that need other keys an exclamation mark, instead of a warning triangle; the AltGr hint badge says Attention. The texts say what may not work and how to avoid it. If you do not type Chinese, Japanese or Korean, the Ctrl+Space note no longer appears.

shortcutKeeper.title: Shortcut Keeper: your shortcuts work in Remote Desktop
shortcutKeeper.description: On Windows, switch on Shortcut Keeper on the Shortcuts page and tick Keep on this PC next to a shortcut: while a Remote Desktop Connection or Windows App session has the keyboard, that shortcut runs Handy Tool on this PC instead of reaching the remote. Every other key still goes to the remote.

updateIndicator.title: The version shows when an update is available
updateIndicator.description: A small arrow next to the version at the bottom left means a newer version is available. Click the version to check for updates with Update now, or to install one that was found.

hotkeyRelease.title: Holding a shortcut no longer keeps a processor core busy
hotkeyRelease.description: On Windows, while you held a shortcut (push-to-talk, for example), Handy Tool checked nonstop whether you had let go, which kept one processor core fully busy. It now checks every 10 ms.

endOfTakeKept.title: The end of a take is kept more reliably
endOfTakeKept.description: When you stop, up to 3 seconds the speech detector had not yet accepted are kept, in the recording and the text, if they hold speech-level sound. Words no longer repeat after a quick restart, and Whisper is less likely to drop a piece's last word.
